The *Sumanabījaniyattheraapadāna* (Tha Ap 476) is a verse text belonging to the Therāpadāna collection of the Pali canon [SuttaCentral]. As part of the biographical poetry of the Buddhist elder monks, it recounts the past karmic deeds and religious career of the thera Sumanabījaniya. SuttaCentral documents five modern translations of the text across five languages [SuttaCentral].

The text also exhibits standard formulaic reuse characteristic of the collection, sharing extended verse runs with other poems in the Therāpadāna, including the *Sumanatālavaṇṭiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 467 and Tha-Ap 380, particularly segments 2.3–7.1), the *Sumanadāmiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 381), and the *Sayampaṭibhāniyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 471) [DharmaNexus]. Beyond Pali, DharmaNexus reports weak computational alignments with the Sanskrit *Kaṭhināvadāna* and the Tibetan *Kāraṇaprajñapti*, though these represent unverified machine matches rather than established textual parallels [DharmaNexus].
